result.topic_en: Notes on biquadratic residues in Gaussian integers: the congruence a−bi ≡ (a+bi)^k modulo a Gaussian prime, worked with the example 1±4i modulo −5+2i, a change of primitive root (logarithms) modulo 5+4i, and powers (x+iy)^{μ+νk} together with the equivalence of exponents μ, ν.

methods.what: Conjugation expressed as a power: a−bi ≡ (a+bi)^k with k²≡1, with example k ≡ 22 mod −5+2i
Numerical example of discrete logarithms modulo −5+2i with base 1+i
Definition of the generalized power (x+iy)^{μ+νk} via norm and the quotient (x+iy)/(x−iy)
Decomposition of the generalized power into powers of x+iy and x−iy
Characterization of (x+iy)^k: norm 1 and same quotient
Change of primitive root: new roots h, H with h^5H^4≡1 mod 5+4i, logarithm condition modulo 41
Solution of the change of root
Equivalence of exponents μ mod p−1, ν mod p+1, equivalently μ+νk mod (a−bk)

items.english: One says that a−bi ≡ (a+bi)^k, with kk ≡ 1.
